races.name: Betway Sprint Handicap

runners_data.name: Kolkata Knight
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good going (form 1) and has similar-going experience; Tom Dascombe runner 37 days off, but this horse's natural instinct to race from the rear will be compromised by a small, speed-packed field where genuine cover at the back simply may not exist.
runners_data.comment: One win in his last five starts, followed by a good second before two below-par efforts set in, and this gelding forced the pace before fading at Sandown last time. Race and ground are both proven from stall seven, and he arrives race-fit, but a couple of underwhelming efforts still need shaking off.

runners_data.name: Zelaina
runners_data.note: K R Burke returns this three-year-old 15 days after a run and has a course-and-distance win on Good, but four consecutive finishes of 8th, 8th, 8th, 24th since that victory raise serious concerns about reproducibility, and the noted tendency to fade in the finish is a direct threat in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of the field on our figures, having managed just one win in her last five starts, with three eighth-place efforts including a keen, too-free reappearance after a break at Ascot. Trip and ground are both proven, but the form that produced that win still needs rediscovering.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope in the plate is a significant positive, and the horse's record of 2 wins and 5 places from 9 starts on similar going is solid; ran only 7 days ago which bears monitoring for residual fatigue, but the form line of 1-3-2 at 5f on Good is the most consistent hold-up profile in the race.
runners_data.comment: This gelding won readily by a length and a quarter off a lower mark at Musselburgh two starts back, before finding last time's step up in grade too sharp. Back down in class and race-fit, he looks capable of bouncing back with a strong pace to suit.

runners_data.name: Wedonttelllies
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes handler is in fair form (T14: 2/25) and the horse has a 5f Good win in recent form; hood headgear noted, and while its true inclination is to come from off the pace, the compressed rear of this race makes that role harder to execute cleanly, tempering confidence.
runners_data.comment: In good form, this gelding was a close third last time on soft ground, beaten only half a length off a mark just 1lb higher than today's. First-time cheekpieces are worth noting, and with trip and ground both proven, he rates a leading threat if the gallop is strong.

runners_data.name: Desert Treasure
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner carrying the weight of two wins from three starts at 5f on Good, making it statistically the sharpest course-and-distance profile in the field; 50 days since last run is the chief concern, and that layoff needs to be respected despite the quality of the trainer.
runners_data.comment: Talented on paper with two wins in her last three starts, but her only subsequent effort - a well-beaten reappearance at York - can be forgiven given a lengthy absence beforehand. She needs to confirm the promise shown as a two-year-old, with the trip proven but potential still to be fulfilled.

runners_data.name: Quantum Power
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a visor, won over this course and distance twice on Good going and has won most recently of the two pace-setters; Jack Callan takes a 3lb claim which partially offsets the weight, and 7 days between runs suggests freshness — the key unknown is whether Percy's Star will fight or capitulate early.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins have this gelding in fine form, the latest a cosy three-quarter-length success off a mark 6lb lower than today's at Windsor. Fitted with a first-time visor and fresh from a run last week, he's open to more, though the tougher mark here is the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Percy's Star
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes over in the saddle for a horse that won last time out at 5f on Good and has shown natural pace throughout its form; Chris Dwyer's team (T14: 0/4) is not in firing form, and dropping from 6f to 5f while running with Quantum Power may prove taxing — the pace duel it enters is the central risk to its chances.
runners_data.comment: This gelding got off the mark readily by three and a half lengths down in trip at Leicester last time, off a mark 8lb below today's. He tops our figures, and with first-time cheekpieces fitted and a yard in good form, the case looks strong, leaving only the stiffer new mark as a concern.

runners_data.name: Ambishio
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby booking Robert Havlin on a horse with two wins at 5f on Standard (AW) rather than Good turf, and the similar-going record of 0 wins from 7 turf starts on comparable conditions is a genuine flag; like Kolkata Knight and Wedonttelllies, this horse's hold-up style will be squeezed in a small field dominated by pace, reducing its chance of finding daylight late.
runners_data.comment: Plenty of raw speed but this gelding remains out of sorts, following a below-par effort at Thirsk last time; his sole win in the last five starts is now five runs back. Trip and ground are proven, though his turf form lags his better efforts on all-weather.

races.paceDynamic: Quantum Power and Percy's Star are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested pace over this five-furlong Newmarket straight. With two horses committed to leading, neither is likely to dictate unchallenged — the early sectionals will be honest to strong on Good to Firm ground, which historically compresses the field and stretches the race out longitudinally rather than bunching at the finish. This shape favours horses who can race prominently just off the two pace-setters and sustain their effort through the closing stages, or free-running types who settle into a rhythm rather than being buried in rear. Prominent racers and those able to track the speed without burning too much early energy hold the clearest edge; true closers face the additional handicap that Kolkata Knight, Wedonttelllies, and Ambishio — all genuine hold-up types — are likely to find themselves unable to secure their natural rearward berth in a small, speed-dominated field, meaning the back of the pack will be unusually congested and late runs off a strong pace even harder to deliver cleanly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Quantum Power and Percy's Star battle for the lead and drain each other, a prominent stalker picking up the pieces wins.
scenarios.body: If Quantum Power and Percy's Star battle for the lead and drain each other, a prominent stalker picking up the pieces wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner (most likely Quantum Power) asserts quickly and Percy's Star cannot match strides, a solo leader controls the race.
scenarios.body: If one front-runner (most likely Quantum Power) asserts quickly and Percy's Star cannot match strides, a solo leader controls the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns exceptionally hot and the field fans wide late, a genuine hold-up type threads through for a late surge.
scenarios.body: If the pace burns exceptionally hot and the field fans wide late, a genuine hold-up type threads through for a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Midfield Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners show early caution or one misses the break and the pace is softer than expected, midfield types strike from a compact field.
scenarios.body: If the two front-runners show early caution or one misses the break and the pace is softer than expected, midfield types strike from a compact field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Quantum Power or Percy's Star flinches first at the break — if Percy's Star misses the start or is immediately outpaced, Quantum Power could steal a soft lead and the contested-pace scenario collapses into a front-runner scenario.

Monitor Mighty Magnus for any signs of the 7-day turnaround affecting its sharpness in the opening furlong; if it travels smoothly in mid-division it becomes the most dangerous hold-up runner in the race given Tudhope's tactical intelligence.

Zelaina's pattern of four consecutive poor finishes after its sole win warrants close attention — if it shows any signs of greenness or reluctance in the stalls or early stages, it is unlikely to overcome that recent form trajectory regardless of the pace shape.

Desert Treasure's 50-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race; William Haggas horses often return fit, but this horse has only three career starts and any ring-rustiness at a fast early tempo on Good to Firm ground will be instantly exposed.

With Kolkata Knight, Wedonttelllies, and Ambishio all naturally wanting to race from the rear, watch the first furlong for congestion and bumping behind the two leaders — any interference or loss of rhythm in that group could effectively remove three runners from meaningful contention.

races.name: Betway Bet 10 Get 40 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Magnetude
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 1m4f on good and on soft, stepping up to 1m6f here; Robert Havlin retains the ride and the horse's natural prominent gate speed makes it the confirmed pace-setter, though it is technically racing slightly out of role relative to its pure style profile.|
runners_data.comment: A progressive colt with two wins in his last five starts, and even when outclassed in a Group 2 last time, the longer trip clearly suited him. Fitted with first-time cheekpieces, he rates a leading threat here, with his level in this grade the main thing to prove.

runners_data.name: Arc Ole Ole
runners_data.note: Two wins in its last three starts including on good ground over 1m4f, and the step to 1m6f looks within range for a horse that travels well close to the pace; Luke Morris is a strong partner for this type of prominent racer and the going is ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, including a battling effort when keeping on from off the pace last time despite having plenty to do, beaten just over three lengths off a mark 4lb below today's. Versatile with trip and ground, he's open to more, with only the sharper mark to overcome.

runners_data.name: Amora Queen
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes over for Charlie Johnston's filly, whose hold-up style is entirely genuine and whose best effort came when finishing second over 1m2f on good going; a big field run at genuine pace would suit but the small seven-runner field here may not generate enough tempo.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, this filly weakened tamely having pulled too hard early at Ascot last time, and today's 14f trip looks a stretch given she's only proven to 10f. The yard has a strong record in this race, but staying the trip is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bay
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson partnered this horse to its most recent win over 1m2f on soft but it has placed on good going before; the step to 1m6f is its furthest trip and Andrew Balding's yard is firing at 9/56 over 14 days, making it a credible prominent threat if the stamina holds.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last five starts, the latest an impressive success over a shorter trip last time, done as if a longer distance would suit, off a mark 7lb below today's. He looks nicely primed to progress again up in trip, but this stiffer new mark is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Lopeo
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch takes the mount for David Menuisier on a hold-up horse that has finished second in both starts at 1m4f and 1m6f on good going — the stamina profile is exactly right for this trip; needs a strong pace to bring its late kick into play, which is not guaranteed in this seven-runner contest.|
runners_data.comment: This gelding confirmed his form when a clear-cut second beaten just two lengths at Doncaster last time, with today's trip and ground both proven. He tops our figures, stays this longer distance well and acts on any ground, making him the one to beat on a competitive mark.

runners_data.name: Hard To Believe
runners_data.note: Trainer Andrew Balding has two runners and Jason Watson rides this horse, which has won twice in its last four starts; a natural front-runner by inclination, it is pushed into a midfield map position here purely because Magnetude and two other prominent types occupy that space — its style efficiency is compromised, temper expectations accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts show plenty of consistency, the latest a narrow neck success off a mark 3lb lower here. He remains open to a little more physical progress, but a fair mark and modest speed figures make him hard to fully fancy in this field.

runners_data.name: Heroics
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 1m6f on good going, which is a live form line for this exact conditions, and David Egan is an astute pilot; however, its front-running tendencies cannot be expressed in this race shape, and Alan King's yard is modestly in form at 3/12 over 14 days — treat its redistributed midfield role as a material disadvantage rather than a neutral factor.|
runners_data.comment: A win up in trip at Sandown last time, doing just enough in front off a mark 3lb below today's, with signs of more in hand. Effective at this trip and racing off a workable weight, he rates a leading threat, with only that workmanlike success a slight query.

races.paceDynamic: Magnetude is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Arc Ole Ole and Mythical Bay as natural prominent types capable of pressuring from the gate, the pace is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than frenetic over this 1m6f trip on good-to-firm ground. Magnetude can dictate from the front without being seriously harassed, setting a rhythm that will suit horses who can travel comfortably in behind and pick up when the tempo increases in the straight. Hard To Believe and Heroics are genuine prominent types by inclination but cannot both secure that position in a field already led by Magnetude and flanked by Arc Ole Ole and Mythical Bay, so they are effectively displaced into midfield roles that are not their natural habitat. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting an honest but not punishing gallop — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with stamina and a clean late turn of foot, particularly those who can travel economically through the race before unleashing in the Newmarket straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Magnetude Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Magnetude leads at a fair but uncontested gallop and the race resolves in the final two furlongs for those who tracked close.
scenarios.body: If Magnetude leads at a fair but uncontested gallop and the race resolves in the final two furlongs for those who tracked close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Magnetude and the prominent group go very steady and the race becomes a sprint finish, enabling the genuine hold-up horses to pounce.
scenarios.body: If Magnetude and the prominent group go very steady and the race becomes a sprint finish, enabling the genuine hold-up horses to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Magnetude Gallops Clear Front
scenarios.trigger: If Magnetude dictates a strong gallop from flag to finish and the field is unable to bridge the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Magnetude dictates a strong gallop from flag to finish and the field is unable to bridge the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Displaced Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Hard To Believe or Heroics, forced out of their natural prominent positions, manage to recover ground and produce a late surge despite their compromised role.
scenarios.body: If Hard To Believe or Heroics, forced out of their natural prominent positions, manage to recover ground and produce a late surge despite their compromised role.

watchPoints.text: Magnetude's early lead is uncontested — if Robert Havlin dictates a very slow pace through the first mile, the race risks turning into a sprint that could be stolen by a horse with superior raw speed rather than stamina.

Hard To Believe and Heroics are both natural prominent runners forced to settle in midfield; watch for either jockey pushing forward early to reclaim a more natural position, which could disrupt Magnetude's rhythm and alter the entire pace dynamic.
Lopeo's two most recent placings are at 1m4f and 1m6f on good going — if Hector Crouch can find a clean passage from a hold-up position, it is better suited to this trip than its OR of 84 implies.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race despite the broader card showing Good — a firmer surface will favour horses with a clean action and recent fast-ground experience, which narrows the field toward Arc Ole Ole and Amora Queen over Mythical Bay's soft-ground form.

races.name: Betway Lancashire Oaks (Fillies' & Mares' Group 2)

runners_data.name: Crepe Suzette
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at 12f on good ground for Gosden, but the step to 14f is unproven and her five most recent runs show she finds one or two too good; tongue-tie and hood suggest a horse that can be held up and produced, and 35 days fresh is ideal.
runners_data.comment: Fit after five weeks off, this filly remains without a win but has been consistent, with two runner-up efforts earlier in this sequence, before a flat effort over a false pace at Carlisle last time. A first-time tongue-tie joins the cheekpieces already tried, and the yard has a strong record here.

runners_data.name: Lava Stream
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes over for O'Meara and she is a genuine hold-up type with a course win at 14f on good; her form tailed off sharply in the second half of last season and a 42-day break plus the recent step back in distance make it harder to be confident she returns to her best.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a York Group 3 last time, having disappointed when ninth four runs back, this mare otherwise races well up to 14f and is suited by this longer trip on any going. Six weeks off is the query, but the yard has a strong record here.

runners_data.name: Miss Justice
runners_data.note: Meehan's mare carries a tongue-tie and her best form has come over shorter — a win at 10f and placed at 10f — so whether she truly stays 14f at Group 2 level is the central question; came off a 20-day turnaround which keeps her sharp.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a Listed race at Chantilly latest - a placing that may have overstated her - this mare has one win from her last five and steps back to a trip that suits. A first-time tongue-tie and a trainer in good form add interest on sound ground.

runners_data.name: Sharpen
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly is a natural front-runner whose OR 96 is the lowest among the prominent types, and 277 days off the track is a significant query; mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the head of affairs, she will likely be racing further back than she would naturally choose.
runners_data.comment: Progressive before a below-form run down at 10f in a Listed race at Cork, her final start of last season, this filly returns up to the 12f that suits with a win from her last five. First-time cheekpieces are added, but a lengthy absence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Tattycoram
runners_data.note: Beckett's four-year-old has solid staying credentials — won over 12f on good at Newmarket and placed at 10-14f — and this is her right trip and ground; a natural prominent racer, she will have to settle in a more restrained position than ideal given the traffic ahead, which slightly complicates the task but her form profile is strong.
runners_data.comment: A Listed winner at Goodwood by a length and a quarter last time, seemingly a step forward for her at three, this filly is a reliable sort who stays 12f and handles any ground. She's below the principals on our figures, though, and needs more to feature.

runners_data.name: Tiffany
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's six-year-old is the race's highest-rated runner and sole confirmed front-runner; her record shows exceptional consistency in defeat (multiple seconds) rather than wins, which is the one reservation, though a visor is fitted and on fast ground at Newmarket leading unchallenged she is a serious force.
runners_data.comment: Second by a short neck in a Listed race at Chantilly on her reappearance, this mare has finished runner-up in all four starts this term and should strip fitter for that seasonal opener. Top-rated here and sharpened by a first-time visor, she just needs her luck to turn.

runners_data.name: Caught U Sleeping
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Noel Meade's yard carrying a 12lb sex allowance advantage, who returns just 10 days after winning a Listed contest over 10f; the step to 14f is uncharted territory but the rapid turnaround suggests connections are confident, and her recent form on good ground is the freshest and most relevant in the race.
runners_data.comment: A close second, beaten just a neck in a Group 3 at Naas latest, this filly is progressive and ran right up to her form there. Suited by 10f on yielding or good ground, she looks sure to be involved again, though the quick turnaround is a query.

runners_data.name: Lady Dora Mae
runners_data.note: Boughey's three-year-old has been remarkably consistent in a short career — five placed efforts at 8-10f on good and soft — and this is both her furthest trip and her first venture into Group company; she is a natural front-runner pushed back by the congested prominent positions, and the open questions of trip and class are significant.
runners_data.comment: A short-head second in a step up to Listed company at Goodwood latest, showing notable progress for the rise in grade, this filly is an ultra-consistent sort with two wins from her last six. She's proven only at 7-10f, though, well short of today's longer trip.

runners_data.name: Lady Roisia
runners_data.note: Beckett's lightly raced three-year-old was last seen pulling up (U) at 12f on good at Newmarket, which is a serious concern that requires explanation; her best form over 7-10f suggests stamina for this distance is unconfirmed, and as a natural prominent type she too will be forced to race more restrained than she prefers.
runners_data.comment: An unseated rider in a Group 2 at Ascot last time undermines a progressive profile that already includes a win in her last four starts, plus a notable step up to Listed level at Newbury previously. This likeable filly, bred for middle distances, is only proven to 10f - short of today's 12f trip.

races.paceDynamic: Tiffany is the sole confirmed front-runner and, as the highest-rated horse in the field at OR 112, she is likely to bowl along at a thoroughly manageable tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Newmarket's July course — a track that rewards those who can control and quicken rather than grind. With no genuine pressure expected from behind, she shapes to dictate a measured, even gallop that keeps the race honest without burning off her own finishing reserves. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically slot in behind her — Tattycoram, Sharpen, Lady Dora Mae and Lady Roisia are all natural prominent racers who will be shuffled into a more restrained position than they would choose, meaning the race shape is largely settled from the outset. A controlled, single-pace gallop at this trip on fast ground with one unchallenged leader favours a horse that can travel close to the pace and produce a sustained late kick — the prominent-to-midfield profile that can get a clear run from two out and has the class to quicken on quick ground is the dominant beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tiffany controls, class tells
scenarios.trigger: If Tiffany dictates an unchallenged even tempo and the race develops into a quality-filtered staying test from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Tiffany dictates an unchallenged even tempo and the race develops into a quality-filtered staying test from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tiffany's lead-from-front style sees her just run out of petrol inside the final furlong on the fast ground after setting a true pace.
scenarios.body: If Tiffany's lead-from-front style sees her just run out of petrol inside the final furlong on the fast ground after setting a true pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Lava Stream or Crepe Suzette get the run of the race from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Lava Stream or Crepe Suzette get the run of the race from well off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front pack collapses, chaos
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed prominent types push forward early and create an uncharacteristically hot pace that collapses the entire front rank in the straight.
scenarios.body: If several redistributed prominent types push forward early and create an uncharacteristically hot pace that collapses the entire front rank in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Tiffany's race record shows a pattern of seconds — watch whether Luke Morris rides her for a win rather than letting her drift into a familiar placed position, as the visor fitting may indicate exactly that intent.

Lady Roisia pulled up on her last run at this course and distance — any market move or absence of market confidence should be noted before settling on race shape, as her scratch or poor run would thin the prominent pack.

Caught U Sleeping runs just 10 days after a Listed win over 10f; if the step to 14f proves a bridge too far she may drop out quickly inside the final quarter-mile and distort the pace picture for those following her.

With Tattycoram, Sharpen, Lady Dora Mae and Lady Roisia all natural prominent types compressed into midfield, watch the early stages — if any of them push forward unexpectedly to claim a prominent berth, the pace dynamic could sharpen materially and hurt Tiffany's chance of a controlled lead.

Good to Firm ground confirmed for the 2:40 slot — any overnight rain or track alteration before racing would disproportionately affect Tiffany, whose best form is on a sounder surface, and would shift probability toward the stamina-reliant hold-up runners.

races.name: Betway Old Newton Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Burdett Road
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse whose recent form shows two top-three finishes at 1m4f-1m5f on Good ground, making this trip and surface an excellent fit; Luke Morris partners him for James Owen whose yard is firing at 9/52 over 14 days, though coming from deep in a steadily run race is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Boasting smart form from overseas, this gelding has yet to match it back in UK handicaps, well below that level when down the field at Ascot last time. He has raced over today's trip and going before and stays 12-14f, so the question is whether he can finally transfer that smart form here.

runners_data.name: Plage De Havre
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter, whose Andrew Balding yard is operating well (12/65 over 14 days); the 52-day absence is worth monitoring on this quicker ground, and her STYLE_FIT flag reflects the structural risk of a horse running into an unusual role — but uncontested control is a real asset.
runners_data.comment: A winner of this race twelve months ago, this gelding travelled strongly before finding one too many, third beaten 5 1/4 lengths in a 12f handicap at York last time. He has raced over today's trip and going before and stays 10-14f; the mark isn't easy, but the profile remains progressive.

runners_data.name: Paddy The Squire
runners_data.note: A genuinely prominent racer with strong credentials at this exact trip and going, boasting three wins and six places in 15 similar-conditions runs; the combination of Iain Jardine's modest recent strike rate (4/40) and Andrew Mullen in the saddle is the mild concern, but his course profile at 1m4f on Good ground is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Held up by traffic problems and left too much to do, this gelding still ran to form when beaten two lengths off a 1lb lower mark at Ascot last time, one of two wins in his last five. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are added, and this longer trip should suit better.

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Has won over 1m4f on Good ground and Silvestre De Sousa is a reliable booking in this grade; the worry is a relatively poor similar-conditions record (12/15 runners beaten) and having just run seven days ago, which could blunt his finishing effort in a race that may be decided by a sharp burst.
runners_data.comment: Impressive when landing a handicap by three and a half lengths off a 5lb lower mark at Windsor last time, this gelding looks to have recaptured last year's smart form and is at home up in front. Top-rated here at 10-12f, he takes plenty of beating on that evidence.

runners_data.name: Klassleader
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a high similar-going strike rate (3/5) who has won twice over 1m2f on Good and placed over 1m6f on Soft, with this 1m4f trip representing a sensible middle ground; Tom Marquand and William Haggas (12/56 in 14 days) is one of the stronger jockey-trainer combinations in the race and the 52-day break looks well-timed.
runners_data.comment: This progressive colt landed a handicap by three lengths on his seasonal debut at York last time, keeping on strongly as if capable of even further, off a mark 8lb below today's. Effective at 12f on good to soft or quick ground, he looks open to more, even up in the weights.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran held-up specialist whose recent turf handicap form on Good ground has been weak (two ninth-place finishes), and Ian Williams's yard is running at just 1/47 over 14 days; the 18-day turnaround is fine, but nothing in his profile screams readiness for a career-best effort.
runners_data.comment: Modestly below form when beaten seven and a half lengths in a tough race at Ascot last time, this gelding has two wins in his last six and goes well on the all-weather nowadays. He stays 12-16f on most surfaces, though a stable short of winners lately and a first-time tongue-tie add question marks.

runners_data.name: Night Breeze
runners_data.note: Has won over 1m2f on Good ground and placed at 1m2f-1m3f, giving a reasonable stamina profile for this 1m4f test; Edward Greatrex takes over from regular connections, which introduces a small unknown, and Ian Williams's slow recent form (1/29) tempers enthusiasm, though his finishing style is exactly right if the pace is falsely run.
runners_data.comment: Second, beaten just over a length when last seen off a mark of 91, this gelding franked that form and is only 4lb higher today, leaving him fairly weighted still. He's effective at 10-12f on most surfaces, but a first-time tongue-tie and a stable short of winners add slight caution.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who has run 1m-1m2f most effectively, and his best form has come on Good ground when able to race forward; compressed into a midfield slot here because the prominent berths are already claimed, he faces a positional challenge that makes his task harder — four-year-old lightly raced, with visor (v) adding a small uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Not far below his form but lacking a bit of resolve when fourth, beaten eight lengths in a handicap at Epsom latest, this gelding remains without a win in five attempts. He stays 10-14f and a step up in trip plus a first-time visor could help, though he needs more resolution to figure.

runners_data.name: Al Aali
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse whose recent form string (00875) tells a story of inconsistency, and his five-run similar-going record shows no wins and just one place; the drop to OR 90 is some compensation but his 1m-1m1f form base raises a question mark about stamina at this trip for a horse that has never won beyond 1m.
runners_data.comment: Matching recent levels when beaten four and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Sandown last time, this gelding is yet to win in five tries and has never gone beyond 10f, a query at this longer trip. First-time cheekpieces and a trainer in form offer some encouragement, with his mark said to look stiff this season.

runners_data.name: Fierce Fortitude
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 1m and placed at 1m2f, so stepping up to 1m4f is an open stamina question — but Kevin Philippart De Foy has him in good hands (2/22 recent, modest but active) and David Egan's booking lends confidence; his form figures on Good ground (2W 3P from 7 runs) make him a live contender if the trip is within range.
runners_data.comment: Roughly matching his form when third, beaten three and a half lengths off a mark of 90 last time, this gelding races off the same mark today. Two wins in his last five is solid enough, but he's best suited at 10f on fast ground and this longer 12f trip brings a stamina question.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: A genuine winner at 1m3f and 1m4f on varying surfaces, with three wins in his last five starts, making this distance a clear strength; true to his prominent, pace-pressing style, he has been mapped to midfield only because the berths ahead are full — his Charlie Johnston/Hector Crouch combination is fair, and if he can reclaim a forward position, his recent winning form demands respect.
runners_data.comment: Stepping forward again when winning a handicap by five lengths off a mark 8lb lower at Hamilton last time, this gelding has three wins from his last five starts and should go well again off the new higher mark. He's suited by 10-11f on a sound surface, with the rising weights the only obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 1m2f on Good ground and shown enough in his last three runs to suggest a return to form, but he is a natural hold-up horse pushed further forward in the map than he will likely race; the James Owen stable has multiple runners today, and Marco Ghiani partners him with the task of producing a late run from what could be a muddling midfield.
runners_data.comment: Denied a clear run late and unlucky not to finish closer than third, beaten 2 1/4 lengths off an unchanged mark last time, this gelding is in excellent form. He's effective at 10-12f on any going, and with our figures well clear of his official mark, he rates a leading threat here.

races.paceDynamic: Plage De Havre is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m4f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to control proceedings at a measured, uncontested gallop that keeps the race well within herself. Paddy The Squire, Claymore, Klassleader, and Fierce Fortitude will push to race prominently behind her, creating a compact early group, while the hold-up brigade of Burdett Road, Enemy, and Night Breeze will settle further back, waiting on developments. The unsustained pace Plage De Havre can dictate on a flat, fair track — where the draw and gallop shape tend to reward those tracking the pace rather than coming from deep — strongly favours horses racing in the prominent-to-midfield bracket who can respond when the tempo lifts in the final quarter-mile; true hold-up horses face a structural disadvantage if the race is never fully run. This field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate cleanly — Ammes, Elsass, and Sportingsilvermine are all natural prominent or forward-going horses compressed into midfield slots they are unlikely to naturally occupy, meaning Paddy The Squire, Claymore, and Klassleader are the most likely to actually secure the prominent positions directly behind Plage De Havre.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Plage De Havre dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is settled in the final 2f with a straight-line quickening burst.
scenarios.body: If Plage De Havre dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is settled in the final 2f with a straight-line quickening burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the steady tempo causes Plage De Havre to set such a slow gallop that the race bunches and turns into a sprint finish off a false pace.
scenarios.body: If the steady tempo causes Plage De Havre to set such a slow gallop that the race bunches and turns into a sprint finish off a false pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If Plage De Havre jumps cleanly, is never pressured, and conserves enough in the tank to outstay rivals with a sustained gallop into the Newmarket July straight.
scenarios.body: If Plage De Havre jumps cleanly, is never pressured, and conserves enough in the tank to outstay rivals with a sustained gallop into the Newmarket July straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Dark Horse
scenarios.trigger: If a congested early battle for prominent positions forces a rougher race, disrupting several fancied runners and creating a gap for a mid-market runner to thread through.
scenarios.body: If a congested early battle for prominent positions forces a rougher race, disrupting several fancied runners and creating a gap for a mid-market runner to thread through.

watchPoints.text: Klassleader (Haggas/Marquand) arrives 52 days fresh with a high similar-going strike rate and has won at this trip — if he travels smoothly just behind Plage De Havre in the first three, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race.

Plage De Havre's 52-day absence on Good to Firm ground (quicker than her usual conditions) could blunt her ability to sustain the gallop into the final two furlongs — watch for her to shorten stride from the 2f pole if not fully tuned.

The cluster of Ammes, Elsass, and Sportingsilvermine — all natural front-runners or prominent types redistributed into midfield — creates a risk of positional jostling leaving the 7f pole; watch for interference or overcrowding as horses seek their natural position in the first half-mile.

Night Breeze is the most interesting hold-up horse if the pace is falsely run; watch how quickly Plage De Havre's lead is cut into at the 3f marker — if the prominent group is still strung out, Night Breeze likely comes too late, but if the field concertinas, he could deliver a late challenge.

Paddy The Squire has the best 1m4f course profile in the field (three wins at the trip on Good ground) and Andrew Mullen will look to position him directly behind the leader — watch his position after the first two furlongs to gauge whether the race is unfolding to his strengths.

races.name: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap

runners_data.name: Zubaru
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong recent form (three wins in last six) and solid record on similar going (9 from 12 qualifiers); races in a control position here and carries 141lbs but the lack of pace pressure is a major structural asset; STYLE_FIT tag is minimal concern when she is likely to be unchallenged for the lead.
runners_data.comment: Zubaru has won three of his last six starts, following up a length win back at 6f off a lower mark at Doncaster just eight days ago. Effective at this trip on quick ground, he heads our figures at 94 and, with the yard in form, rates the one to beat despite a first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a solid 6f handicap profile and two wins from 15 similar-going runs; returns after 42 days off which is worth monitoring, but Tom Marquand's booking adds confidence; consistent second and third positions over this exact trip suit a scenario where Zubaru sets a comfortable tempo.
runners_data.comment: Jonny Concrete has hit the frame in three of his last five starts, with an underwhelming run and a flat ninth among the exceptions, and was beaten just three lengths off a lower mark at York last time. Effective at this trip regardless of going, he gets first-time cheekpieces and a notable jockey booking, with our figures rating him a leading threat at 90 despite the stable's recent lull.

runners_data.name: Golden Long
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner whose last win came over 6f on Good going, aligning well with today's conditions; Hector Crouch takes the ride for a trainer with a quiet 14-day strike rate, and the step back from softer surface outings last time makes this a more natural fit.
runners_data.comment: Golden Long won by a length and a quarter off a lower mark at Windsor two starts back, but he raced too freely and faded on easier ground last time, back on the same mark here. A former Hong Kong campaigner who remains hard to assess, he wants a sound surface at this minimum trip, and with a first-time tongue-tie added, the case is only lukewarm.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this hold-up filly who has a win over this exact course and distance in similar going; her hold-up style is genuinely natural and she is the most credible late-finishing threat if the pace sets up correctly, though in a Zubaru-controlled race she may need a strong tempo she is unlikely to get.
runners_data.comment: Yes I'm Mali's form has been patchy - a half-length win off a lower mark at Thirsk back in April sits alongside a couple of well-beaten efforts either side of it - and he may have been drawn on the wrong side last time out. Suited by this minimum trip on a sound surface, he rates no more than an each-way chance on his up-and-down record.

runners_data.name: Em Four
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form shows a drop back to 6f from 5f starts and a modest sim-going record (0 wins from 15); William Carver is an apprentice, which slightly elevates the uncertainty; best suited to a scenario where the pack presses Zubaru hard early.
runners_data.comment: Em Four's standout form came back in April, a two-and-a-half-length win off a lower mark at Wolverhampton, but he has struggled to land a blow since that mark rose and was undone by a sluggish beginning last time. A front-running sort who wants this minimum trip on a sound surface, he needs the gallop to suit and rates hard to fancy at 72 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rajaking
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a decent record on Good ground at 6f and one recent win at this trip; Jack Callan claims 3lb, and his last two runs were disappointing, but a genuinely fast pace — which is not the likely shape here — would be needed to bring him into play late.
runners_data.comment: Rajaking remains without a win in his last five starts, though his latest effort was an improvement on his second run back on turf, beaten just two lengths off a higher mark at Windsor. His mark is easing but probably needs to drop further, and he wants this minimum trip on a sound surface, with a first-time tongue-tie added for a modest each-way threat at best.

runners_data.name: Dancing Rinca
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity returning after a 260-day absence for a trainer with a 0/6 14-day record; racing style is unconfirmed (tagged UNKNOWN), and the long layoff on lightly-raced profile makes this a significant risk factor regardless of how the race develops.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Rinca has not raced for 260 days, and his last two starts before this absence were already well below his one-time smart form in the US, beaten seven lengths in a claiming event at Santa Anita last time. Effective around this trip on quick ground, he needs this outing after such a lengthy break and is hard to support at 67 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with headgear (blinkers noted) returning 15 days after his last run; sim-going record is 0 wins from 15, and recent 6f efforts have been well beaten; at OR=73 he needs exceptional circumstances to feature, and his profile does not suit a Zubaru-led controlled race.
runners_data.comment: Dashing Dick returned to form when a close third, front-running for a three-quarter-length defeat off today's mark right here last time, having managed only two eighth-place efforts before that. Effective across this trip on most types of going, he adds first-time blinkers and could go well again if allowed to dictate up front, rating a leading contender at 89 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Emperor's Son
runners_data.note: In-form runner (136941 recent form) whose natural hold-up style has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is loaded with closers; Warren Fentiman (3) claims, and while his last win came over 6f on Good ground, racing outside his preferred position at the rear is a meaningful structural disadvantage today.
runners_data.comment: Emperor's Son won by a neck off a lower mark at Hamilton last time, form since franked by the runner-up's subsequent efforts, and he may be nicely treated as a result. Suited by this minimum trip on a sound surface, he offers more upside than his eighth-placed figure of 79 suggests.

runners_data.name: Distant Rumble
runners_data.note: Two recent wins and a placed run show genuine current form, but as a true hold-up horse pushed forward on the map by field congestion, he will struggle to replicate his natural finishing kick from a more prominent position than he prefers; Jason Watson is a capable handler of tactical situations but the pace shape here is working against him.
runners_data.comment: Distant Rumble ran to form when third, beaten just three-quarters of a length off a 70 mark last time, and returns on the same mark today. Suited by this trip on most types of going, he is in excellent heart, with the static mark the only nagging concern against a field he matches well on our figures at 88.

races.paceDynamic: Zubaru is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control the pace from the front at a tempo of her own choosing on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. The prominent types — Jonny Concrete, Golden Long, and Em Four — will press up behind but none is likely to force a truly scorching pace, meaning Zubaru can bowl along at a sustainable gallop and dictate throughout. This shape strongly favours the horse who can lead or sit just off a solo pace-setter and quicken from the front two furlongs out, which points to front-running and prominent profiles having a material structural edge; hold-up horses will need an unusually strong pace collapse to get into this race late. The field contains more hold-up runners than the map can properly accommodate — Emperor's Son and Distant Rumble are genuine closers who will be compelled to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, compromising their natural ability to deliver a late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zubaru Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zubaru gets away cleanly and no prominent rival applies early pressure, she dictates the pace from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: If Zubaru gets away cleanly and no prominent rival applies early pressure, she dictates the pace from flag to finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Collects Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group behind Zubaru races keenly and pushes the pace beyond her comfort zone, tightening the finish.
scenarios.body: If the prominent group behind Zubaru races keenly and pushes the pace beyond her comfort zone, tightening the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front rank ties up inside the final furlong, opening a lane for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front rank ties up inside the final furlong, opening a lane for hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes Blind
scenarios.trigger: If chaos at the break scrambles the pace shape, an exposed runner finds a gap that their rating does not normally justify.
scenarios.body: If chaos at the break scrambles the pace shape, an exposed runner finds a gap that their rating does not normally justify.

watchPoints.text: Zubaru's weight (141lbs) is the principal risk factor — if she labours in the final furlong under top weight having led throughout, Jonny Concrete or Golden Long are positioned to cut her down.

Emperor's Son and Distant Rumble are genuine closers forced to race closer to the pace than ideal; if either settles poorly or gets caught in traffic mid-race, their recent form figures will be flattering and their actual chance in this shape materially reduced.

Dancing Rinca's 260-day absence combined with an unknown style profile makes her a genuine market mover risk — monitor market moves in the final 30 minutes before post time for any significant support.

The Good to Firm going across all races on the card is confirmed and consistent; no significant watering appears to have altered the surface mid-card, so pace times from earlier races can be used as a reliable benchmark for whether Zubaru's lead is truly sustainable.

Jonny Concrete has the most consistent finishing record over 6f on similar going in this field (11 from 15) and could be the primary beneficiary if Zubaru's advantage narrows inside the final furlong — watch how Marquand positions him in the first two furlongs.

races.name: Betway Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap

runners_data.name: One Smack Mac
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Jamie Osborne with solid 7f form on good ground (2nd and 3rd from seven similar-going runs); back 17 days from a poor effort, the headgear note and 0-from-last-five form is a concern, but if the pace truly tests the leaders he has the profile to close.
runners_data.comment: One Smack Mac remains without a win in his last five starts, his latest effort fading late in a big, high-class handicap after being niggled along too soon. He acts well on heavy or good ground, with his below-par runs on quicker going excusable, and wears a first-time hood, but a lengthy spell without any sign of form leaves him hard to trust at 88.

runners_data.name: Houquetot
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners this hold-up type returning from 49 days off for James Owen, whose yard is running at a sharp 9/52 in the last 14 days; five of his last six runs have been over 7-8f on good ground with modest results and no wins, making him hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Houquetot's latest was an educational reappearance run, yet he still battled on for a long way before fading to a five-and-a-quarter-length defeat in a handicap at Newbury. He was successful in a Group event in France and has yet to reproduce that level for his new yard, but this run should have put him spot on, with this trip on soft or good ground suiting well.

runners_data.name: Silver Ghost
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride on this prominent racer for Emma Lavelle, who has excellent course-compatible form — 2nd and 3rd from his last two 7f good-ground runs; 13 of 14 similar-going starts show he handles conditions well, making him the natural prominent beneficiary of No Retreat's pace.
runners_data.comment: Silver Ghost ran to form when beaten only a neck off a lower mark right here at Newmarket last time, despite a sluggish getaway costing her momentum early. Still without a win in this sequence, she clearly holds claims back on the same assessment, is suited by this trip on a sound surface, and rates a leading contender at 104 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Akkadian Thunder
runners_data.note: David Tudhope's mount for David O'Meara has a strong recent record at 7f on good ground, but his natural hold-up style means he has been pushed into a midfield mapping in a field this congested at the rear — his 0.93 style-fit rating reflects genuine positional compromise and tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Akkadian Thunder was beaten three and a half lengths off today's mark at York last time, in a performance that matched his current form. He remains without a win in this sequence but is clearly capable when conditions fall his way, acts on a range of going at this trip, and rates a leading contender at 105 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Divine Libra
runners_data.note: Jack Callan (3lb claimer) partners this prominent-style runner for Charles Hills, back after 59 days; best form has come at 6f and the step up to 7f on fast ground is not certain to suit, though his two 7f good-ground placed efforts suggest he is not inconvenienced by the trip.
runners_data.comment: Divine Libra was unable to land a blow from a wide stall last time, beaten three lengths off a higher mark at Chester, and he still has a point to prove in this grade. He is versatile with the going across this sort of trip, remains without a win in this sequence, but the runner-up effort earlier in the sequence hints he retains ability at 96 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Goldmoyne
runners_data.note: Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) rides this genuine front-running/prominent type for James Owen, but with No Retreat, Silver Ghost and others occupying the prime positions, Goldmoyne is unlikely to secure his natural berth — the redistribution to a midfield mapping is a material discount to his chance here.
runners_data.comment: Goldmoyne performed right at his peak when beaten only a nose off a lower mark at Doncaster last time, continuing a fairly consistent record that includes a win earlier in this sequence. He looks fairly treated on his current mark, is versatile with conditions across this trip range, and adds first-time cheekpieces as he rates a leading threat at 103 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Golden Redemption
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson rides Andrew Balding's consistent hold-up performer whose recent form shows three placed efforts from five good-ground 7f starts — a genuine hold-up type repositioned to midfield on the map due to field congestion, which dilutes the value of his strong similar-going record.
runners_data.comment: Golden Redemption was a shade disappointing when beaten four lengths off a higher mark right here last time, though the placed effort before that suggested he was nicely treated. The stable has a strong record in this event, having landed it twelve months ago, and he is suited by this trip on a sound surface, but the latest form is a slight worry for a colt without a win in this sequence.

runners_data.name: No Retreat
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners the top-rated horse in the race (OR 107, 144lbs) for George Scott, a proven front-runner who has won twice and placed nine times on good ground — his 0.92 style-fit note reflects that his pace role is confirmed, though the significant weight burden late over 7f is the key risk factor.
runners_data.comment: No Retreat's latest run can be forgiven, as trouble in running left him unplaced in a competitive big-field handicap. Normally a model of consistency, he faces a stiff task again off his current mark but remains well suited to this trip and going, with the stable in good form.

runners_data.name: Crown Board
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the mount for Jane Chapple-Hyam but this hold-up type has been off 126 days and shows zero placed efforts from eight good-ground runs in his last-five history — the layoff combined with a poor going record makes him extremely difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: Crown Board's form dates to a half-length handicap victory off a lower mark at Chelmsford in December, with modest efforts at Meydan and Abu Dhabi since. He is feasibly well treated on last year's best form, acts on any going and is suited by this trip, though a near four-month absence adds a slight query.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Jason Watson rides this prominent-style runner for Michael Appleby, back just 14 days from his last run; best form has come over 6f (one win) and his three most recent 7f efforts have yielded a 5th, 4th and 13th — the slight trip-stretch concern is real though he has the pace profile to travel prominently with No Retreat.
runners_data.comment: Royal Zabeel is already a Listed winner and was going well before his below-par effort, beaten 10 lengths in a big-field handicap at Ascot last time, seemingly compromised by how that race split. Dropped back to 7f, where he is effective on a sound surface, he tops our figures at 107 and remains the one to beat, with only the yard's recent lull to note.

races.paceDynamic: No Retreat is the confirmed lone front-runner and, carrying top weight of 144lbs off OR 107, will dictate from the outset over Newmarket's July course 7f on Good to Firm ground — a surface and track where he has won twice and placed nine times from fourteen starts. With no genuine rival willing to press him early, he is set to control a sustainable gallop that will suit horses travelling prominently in his wake rather than those required to make up ground from the rear. The field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate naturally: Akkadian Thunder and Golden Redemption are genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield, while Goldmoyne is a true prominent racer who will struggle to secure that position with No Retreat, Silver Ghost, Divine Libra and Royal Zabeel all ahead of him. The tactical verdict is clear: a measured, front-runner-controlled tempo on fast ground at Newmarket favours prominent racers who can track the pace and pick up in the straight, rather than hold-up horses who will have too much ground to cover on a track that rewards forward positioning.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If No Retreat is allowed to roll along unchallenged and sets a strong but measured pace that softens out hold-up types.
scenarios.body: If No Retreat is allowed to roll along unchallenged and sets a strong but measured pace that softens out hold-up types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If No Retreat's top weight tells late and a close-tracking prominent horse collars him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If No Retreat's top weight tells late and a close-tracking prominent horse collars him inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Gets Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the race gets strung out, creating gaps for a midfield mover to thread through in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong and the race gets strung out, creating gaps for a midfield mover to thread through in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If No Retreat produces an unexpectedly fast early sectional that causes prominent types to over-race and creates late opportunities for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: If No Retreat produces an unexpectedly fast early sectional that causes prominent types to over-race and creates late opportunities for hold-up runners.

watchPoints.text: No Retreat (Tom Marquand) sets off in front — if he jumps cleanly and gets across unchallenged in the first furlong, the race shape is effectively set and prominent trackers Silver Ghost and Royal Zabeel become the key dangers.

Silver Ghost's jumping position from the stalls is critical: David Egan must get him into a tracking position behind No Retreat within the first two furlongs to exploit the prominent profile that suits this race shape.

Goldmoyne's jockey Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) will face an immediate decision about whether to push forward aggressively or accept a midfield berth — forcing the position risks burning him out early; accepting midfield runs against his natural style.

Crown Board's 126-day absence for Jane Chapple-Hyam is the longest layoff in the field and his Good-to-Firm going record shows no placed efforts — monitor market moves as a late withdrawal risk or significant drifter.

The Good to Firm official going (confirmed across multiple races on the card) rewards horses with a prominent position and a clean turn of foot in the final two furlongs — any horse drawn wide that fails to secure an early prominent berth will be racing against the grain of the track bias.

races.name: Betway Launches Super Sub Handicap

runners_data.name: Proud Nation
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong similar-going credentials (3/4, 1W3P) at 7f; Richard Fahey yard in solid form at T14 6/56; 21 days since last run is a manageable fresher; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a genuine weight advantage in a competitive handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Proud Nation performed to expectations on his handicap debut, beaten three lengths off a higher mark at Chester last time, continuing a genuinely consistent record that includes a win in this sequence. A nice sort who handles some cut in the ground as well as good going, he is suited by this trip, though his figures leave him towards the bottom of this field at 83.

runners_data.name: Ironwill
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with five runs at 6-7f on good ground and an impressive 1W3P similar-going profile; Stuart Williams yard quiet at T14 0/23 which is a mild concern; has the tactical pace to sit just behind I'll Be Back and capitalise if the leader tires.|
runners_data.comment: Ironwill arrives on the back of two wins in his last five starts and ran to form again when beaten two and a half lengths off this same mark at Sandown last time, only his second try at this trip. Not quite at his sharpest over 7f in those two runs but a picture of consistency throughout, he tops our figures at 94 and, despite the yard's recent lull, rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Alaminos
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old has excellent similar-going form (5/5, 1W2P) at 6f but is stepping up to 7f here; a natural prominent racer who is likely to find himself unable to secure his preferred pitch given I'll Be Back's dominance, which tempers his chance despite strong going figures.|
runners_data.comment: Alaminos looked well below his true level in a handicap at York last time, a run that jars with an otherwise solid recent record including a win in this sequence. Sharper form prior suggests he can bounce back if this longer trip suits, and he is best served by a sound surface, but he sits bottom of these figures at 78 with the stable out of sorts.

runners_data.name: Lightning Polka
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up from 6f with blinkers; 64 days off the track is the most notable concern, and only 3/5 on similar going with one win at the trip; Ed Walker in fair form at T14 7/27 but the layoff and trip extension create genuine questions.|
runners_data.comment: Lightning Polka became unsettled following an awkward start and trailed the field in a handicap right here last time, a display that undersells her better recent form including a win in this sequence. Fairly treated on her form as a juvenile, she has a stamina query at this longer trip but is suited by give in the ground, and now wears a first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' runner is a natural prominent type who will likely be shuffled back from his natural position with I'll Be Back dictating; 10 days since last run suggests fitness, but 0W from six similar-going runs and a style-fit discount make this a tough assignment even if he gets a good trip.|
runners_data.comment: Aqua Bear performed up to expectations over this sort of trip when beaten three lengths off this same mark at Carlisle last time, part of a largely dependable record that includes a win in this sequence. Versatile with the ground across this trip range, he is fancied to give another honest account and rates a leading threat at 90 on our figures.

runners_data.name: I'll Be Back
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and top weight on OR 92 with an unbeaten two-from-two record; K R Burke is in solid form at T14 7/55 and Sam James is a strong booking; 82 days since last run is the only flag, though both prior wins came on similar fast ground and the style-fit note reflects his mapped position rather than any fundamental concern.|
runners_data.comment: I'll Be Back is unbeaten in two starts, following up a short break with a comfortable length victory in a strong novice event at Leicester, form since franked emphatically by that race's form. With signs he'll stay beyond this trip, he looks sure to progress again on testing or better ground, though the lengthy absence since that win adds a note of caution at 92 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Winding Stream
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' runner is stepping back from 8-10f trips to 7f and has only 2/4 on similar going with no wins or places on good; Hector Crouch takes the ride and the return to a shorter trip could sharpen him up, but the absence of a win on good ground is a meaningful form query.|
runners_data.comment: Winding Stream was ridden prominently and found little, beaten four and a quarter lengths in a high-class handicap at Ascot last time, but this looks a notably easier opportunity than his recent novice company and he could yet improve on his mark. The stable has been successful in two of the last three runnings of this race, and with this trip well within range on a sound surface, he rates a leading threat at 94 on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: I'll Be Back is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field over Newmarket's straight July course, this race will be run at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front. I'll Be Back is unbeaten in two starts and has the class advantage on OR 92, meaning Sam James can dictate from the gates, set honest fractions without being harassed, and control the pace through the early and middle stages before quickening or grinding clear. Ironwill and Winding Stream will track closely from prominent positions, creating a compressed mid-race shape rather than a true test of stamina. This field contains more genuine prominent-racing types than the pace map can accommodate — Alaminos and Aqua Bear are natural front-runners or close trackers who are likely to find themselves racing slightly off their preferred position, conceding early ground to I'll Be Back and the confirmed prominent holders. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off a controlled leader and sprint late, or a classy front-runner who is never headed — in Good to Firm conditions on a flat, undemanding track, a patient hold-up or close-tracking finisher who can exploit a steady early gallop is the profile to follow.

watchPoints.text: I'll Be Back's 82-day absence is the single biggest risk factor — watch the pre-race market move closely; if he drifts significantly it signals connections have reservations about his fitness after the break.

Alaminos and Aqua Bear are both natural prominent types who may contest for early positions despite being mapped to midfield — any scrimmaging in the first two furlongs could compromise both their chances and disrupt Ironwill's tracking run.

Lightning Polka's 64-day layoff combined with the step up to 7f and blinkers headgear creates a fitness and tactical unknown — watch how Tom Marquand positions her early; if she is pushed forward it suggests the stable expects her to need the lead rather than settle.

Proud Nation is drawn with no stall disadvantage on this straight course and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is live value in a seven-runner field; watch for her to be produced wide and late if the pace is truly controlled.|
